message.content:
A cell that contains more than one nucleus is called a **multinucleated cell**.  
In biology this is often referred to as a **syncytium** (plural *syncytia*).  

Examples of syncytial cells include:

| Cell type | Typical function | Where it occurs |
|-----------|-----------------|-----------------|
| **Skeletal muscle fiber** | Contraction | Muscles |
| **Osteoclast** | Bone resorption | Bone tissue |
| **Placental syncytiotrophoblast** | Nutrient exchange | Placenta |
| **Multinucleated giant cells** | Immune response (e.g., Langhans giant cells in granulomas) | Inflammatory lesions |

So, if you’re looking for a single word, “syncytium” (or “multinucleated giant cell” when referring to immune cells) is the term you’re after.
